text_en: Dead flies make the perfumer’s ointment give off a foul odor; so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
text_cn: 一个死苍蝇能败坏一碗制香膏者的香膏；一点愚昧也能败坏智慧和尊荣。

text_en: The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.
text_cn: 智慧人的心倾向右，愚人的心偏向左。

text_en: Even when fools walk on the road, they lack sense, and show to everyone that they are fools.
text_cn: 愚人连在走路时，也是无知，并称众人皆糊涂。

text_en: If the anger of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your post, for calmness will undo great offenses.
text_cn: 若当权者向你生气，你不可离弃岗位，因为心平气和能避免大错。

text_en: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as great an error as if it proceeded from the ruler:
text_cn: 我在太阳下见了一件不幸的事，似乎是出于掌权者的错误：

text_en: folly is set in many high places, and the rich sit in a low place.
text_cn: 愚人占居高位，贵人屈居下位。

text_en: I have seen slaves on horseback, and princes walking on foot like slaves.
text_cn: 我看见仆人骑马，而王侯反像仆人一样步行。

text_en: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a snake.
text_cn: 挖掘陷阱的必自陷其中，拆毁墙壁的必被蛇咬伤；

text_en: Whoever quarries stones will be hurt by them; and whoever splits logs will be endangered by them.
text_cn: 开凿石头的必为石压伤，砍伐树木的必遭遇危险。

text_en: If the iron is blunt, and one does not whet the edge, then more strength must be exerted; but wisdom helps one to succeed.
text_cn: 铁器钝了，如不将刃磨快，必费许多气力；成功是智慧的效能。

text_en: If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no advantage in a charmer.
text_cn: 行法术之前，就已被蛇咬伤，法术于行法术的人，就没有好处。

text_en: Words spoken by the wise bring them favor, but the lips of fools consume them.
text_cn: 智者口中的语言，为人有益；愚人的口舌却自招灭亡：

text_en: The words of their mouths begin in foolishness, and their talk ends in wicked madness;
text_cn: 他口中的语言，开始是愚昧，最后却是残忍的狂语。

text_en: yet fools talk on and on. No one knows what is to happen, and who can tell anyone what the future holds?
text_cn: 愚人只知多言：“将来的事怎样，人不知道；人身后的事，有谁来告诉他？”

text_en: The toil of fools wears them out, for they do not even know the way to town.
text_cn: 愚人以劳碌为烦恼，因为连怎样进城，他也不知道。

text_en: Alas for you, O land, when your king is a servant, and your princes feast in the morning!
text_cn: 邦国，你的君王若是一个幼童，你的长官若清晨宴饮，你就有祸了！

text_en: Happy are you, O land, when your king is a nobleman, and your princes feast at the proper time— for strength, and not for drunkenness!
text_cn: 邦国，你的君王若出身显贵，你的长官若宴饮有时，只求养身，不为快乐，那你就有福了。

text_en: Through sloth the roof sinks in, and through indolence the house leaks.
text_cn: 屋顶坍塌，由于怠惰；房屋滴漏，由于手懒。

text_en: Feasts are made for laughter; wine gladdens life, and money meets every need.
text_cn: 设宴是为欢乐，酒可使生活愉快；钱能应付一切。

text_en: Do not curse the king, even in your thoughts, or curse the rich, even in your bedroom; for a bird of the air may carry your voice, or some winged creature tell the matter.
text_cn: 在床榻上，不要诅咒君王；在卧室内，不要咒骂长官，因为空中的飞鸟能传音，有翅翼的能传话。
